handoff.verdict: Fixed-source two-route real WebGL2 GPU functional smoke passed on the second attempt. Accept the second attempt only as side-entry functional evidence. Process compliance is not established: attempt 0 produced software WebGL and failed, then a renderer switch/retry produced the GPU pass, which violates the stop boundary. This is not a quality acceptance, not a full-match acceptance and not acceptance of the three standards.
handoff.firstStep: dot-B first verifies sourceCommit/sourceTree and checks the SHA-256 of every published file against artifact-hashes.json, then publishes the after route as a side entry and confirms the site version it lands on.
doNot: Do not use this run to change the default entry.
Do not treat it as a six-round full match, halftime side switch, end-of-match or play-again, or human visual/feel/audio acceptance.

Do not treat the single initial deployment view as coverage of the wall face/corner, cover sightline, lamp readability, enemy contrast or combat view; the deployment menu and HUD overlay much of that frame and it cannot verify the three-piece quality.
Do not claim cross-task GPU exclusivity or Node 24+ validation.
Do not claim the first attempt was the prescribed native configuration or that no renderer switch occurred.

Do not claim preview/port/parent-chain cleanup or full serial verification between the two attempts; partial process-sample evidence covers 20:43:30.363-20:44:29.306Z (only the receiver worker), while the last ~30.34s and port state are unknown.
Do not use the second attempt's success to erase the stop-boundary violation.

processGaps.stopBoundaryViolation: Attempt 0 produced software WebGL and exited 1 (default headless shell; FPS_SMOKE_CHROMIUM unset; exact FPS_SMOKE_RENDERER value not retained). A second invocation then switched to full Chromium with FPS_SMOKE_RENDERER=native and obtained a GPU pass. That is a renderer switch and retry after a non-GPU result, contrary to the original card's keep-result/no-switch/no-retry rule. Pre-specifying an existing executable in the second invocation does not override the already-triggered stop condition.
processGaps.firstAttemptRecords: Attempt 0 run id 9a5c02fc6b51-wS6MkO; output directory outputs/art-standards-smoke/9a5c02fc6b51-wS6MkO (repository-relative). The runner produced a manifest and two report.json files per its source. The complete manifest stdout is retained in the local first-attempt smoke log; the earlier cited 2.5 KB stdout fragment is only the tail of this same log. Its redacted full content is published in exit-evidence.json attempts[0].manifest and first-attempt-and-gaps.json firstAttempt.manifest, and its 21 build hashes are identical to the second attempt's published build list. Not retained: the output-directory report.json contents, browser logs and the raw report.webgl version/renderer/vendor/unmaskedVendor.
processGaps.firstAttemptCleanup: The explicit preview TCP/port-close proof is not retained. Browser exits are known (96172/50524 exit 0), and runner smoke-backlog 90404 returned rc=1 at 20:43:30.074Z, but the exit code/time of in-process smoke.mjs 111052 and the identity/exit of outer parent 6792 remain unknown; 37504's own exit code is not separately retained (offline-base route status 0). Browser exit 0 is still not a substitute for preview/parent-chain teardown. Partial process-sample evidence: pid 50524 sampled to 20:43:29.256Z, pid 111052 to 20:43:29.499Z, pid 90404 to 20:43:29.492Z, and offline-base route smoke.mjs pid 37504 sampled 20:39:43.914-20:41:11.233Z; all are absent from samples from 20:43:30.363Z, consistent with exit.
processGaps.betweenAttempts: Partial process-sample evidence exists through 20:44:29.306Z: a browser-scoped Win32_Process polling log (20:41:35.966-20:44:29.306Z) and a node-scoped log (20:39:39.501-20:44:27.390Z) show pid 50524 last at 20:43:29.256Z and pids 111052/90404 last at 20:43:29.499Z/20:43:29.492Z; from 20:43:30.363Z to 20:44:29.306Z all samples contain only receiver worker pid 78372, with no own browser/smoke/vite process. There is no port/listener probe. 20:44:29.306-20:44:59.647Z (~30.34s) and the exit status of 111052/6792 are unknown. Cleanup after the second run cannot prove the first attempt was clean.
